title: bee-chain-nudge + bee-state-sync hooks incl. worktree-holds renewal, conformance
action: Port the two heavy hooks whose dependencies are now all in Rust, onto the rust-port-7 hook runtime: (1) bee-chain-nudge — SubagentStop advisory JSON (worker-collect nudge when a bee worker or swarming phase, review-synthesis nudge, scribing-debt warning) built on the already-ported state/cells readers; silent when nothing applies. (2) bee-state-sync — throttled heartbeat touch, reservation lease renewal, cross-worktree hold renewal (port the remaining worktree-holds renewal path), and the locked rebuildStateProjection call from rust-port-16 with LOCK_BUSY skipping silently (msn-7 F8: never writes workflow records); completely silent, always exit 0. RIG NOTE (the rig is NOT a shared module): the conformance discipline lives duplicated in-file — copy the seeded-root, sha256-oracle-verification, node-verdict-non-triviality, twin-pairing and negative-control helpers from crates/queen-bee/tests/hook_conformance.rs (the rig of record), exactly as crates/queen-bee/tests/modelguard_conformance.rs did. Build ONE target heavyhooks_conformance: advisory-text parity for chain-nudge across its trigger classes and silence classes; for state-sync, side-effect parity — the state.json rebuild result, heartbeat/lease/hold renewals, and the LOCK_BUSY skip — plus crash fail-open on both.

truths: cargo --test heavyhooks_conformance runs and reports at least 12 passed, fixture names listed per class
chain-nudge advisory JSON matches node byte-for-byte across trigger classes, and both runtimes stay silent on the silence classes
state-sync side effects (state.json rebuild, heartbeat, lease and hold renewals) match node on the same fixtures; LOCK_BUSY skips silently on both
crash fixtures exit 0 with a hooks.jsonl crash line on both runtimes

artifacts.substantive: chain-nudge and state-sync hooks plus heavyhooks_conformance corpus

trace.outcome: Rework round (goal-check judge NEEDS_REVISION, 4 findings, all fixed with red-first proof): (1) run_fail_open now threads the caller's real hook name instead of a hardcoded file-level constant, fixing a genuine cross-hook crash-log divergence (also fixed model_guard.rs's pre-existing instance of the same bug per the coordinator's note); crash tests now assert hook-field equality cross-runtime. (2) added a real workflow-record fixture + a new test proving state-sync's AUTHORITATIVE rebuild branch (not just the no-op fall-through) matches the mjs oracle; renamed the old mis-scoped test. (3) added the missing cross-runtime hold-ledger comparison. (4) replaced every store-file parsed-Value comparison with a byte-level (key-order-sensitive) comparator, since IndexMap's PartialEq ignores order under this workspace's preserve_order feature -- added a permanent meta-test proving it. heavyhooks_conformance.rs stays at 16 tests, now materially stronger.
deviations: Rework round (independent goal-check judge: NEEDS_REVISION, fixability automatic). Four findings, all fixed:
1. Crash-log hook-name divergence (real behavior bug, not just a coverage
gap): `run_fail_open` (write_guard.rs) hardcoded `adapter::log_crash`'s
hook-name argument to this file's own `HOOK_NAME` constant
("write-guard"), so a chain-nudge or state-sync panic logged
`"hook":"write-guard"` in `.bee/logs/hooks.jsonl` instead of the real
crashing hook's name — the node oracle's `logCrash(root, hookName, ...)`
never has this problem, since it takes the calling hook's name as a
parameter. Fixed by threading `hook_name: &str` through `run_fail_open`
and updating every caller (write_guard, model_guard, chain_nudge,
state_sync) plus 4 pre-existing direct-call test sites that previously
passed no hook name at all (writeguard_core.rs, writeguard_read.rs,
writeguard_bash.rs, modelguard_conformance.rs — the last of these was
itself silently asserting the wrong hook name for a model-guard crash
test before this fix, though no prior assertion actually checked the
`hook` field value to notice). Both crash tests in
heavyhooks_conformance.rs now assert the `hook` field cross-runtime,
not merely an `error` substring.
2. State-sync's authoritative rebuild was never proved — only the
no-workflow-records fall-through was. The original "idle_bootstrap" test
named a branch (state_projection.rs's authoritative idle-bootstrap path)
it never actually constructed: with zero workflow records seeded, every
fixture always took the `apply_overrides_only` fall-through. Fixed by:
(a) renaming that test to
`state_sync_no_workflow_records_only_refreshes_overrides_matches_oracle`
and adding an explicit "phase stays idle, feature stays unset" assertion
proving it really is the fall-through; (b) adding a new `workflow`
fixture op (`tests/support/heavyhooks_fixture.mjs`, via the real
`workflow-store.mjs` `createWorkflow`) and a new test,
`state_sync_authoritative_idle_bootstrap_adopts_active_workflow_matches_oracle`,
that seeds a genuine active workflow record and asserts
phase/feature/mode/summary/next_action/approved_gates are adopted from
it — cross-runtime, byte-level — proving the authoritative branch this
cell's hook exists to route through.
3. The hold row was the only one of the four renewed records (session,
claim, lease, hold) with no cross-runtime comparison at all — only prose
guarded `holds.rs`'s typed `Hold` round-trip against the exact
null-injection risk the session write path was fixed for in the prior
pass. Fixed by adding a cross-runtime byte-level assertion on the hold
ledger file in the renewal test.
4. All four store-file comparisons (state.json, session.json, claim.json,
lease file, hold ledger) previously compared PARSED `serde_json::Value`s.
This workspace's `preserve_order` feature backs `Value`'s `Map` with an
`IndexMap`, and `IndexMap`'s `PartialEq` compares as a SET — it
deliberately ignores key order — so a key-order (or formatting)
divergence in a written store file was invisible to every prior
assertion in this suite, exactly the class of bug D3 (byte
compatibility) exists to catch (and the exact thing rust-port-15's own
rework found two real instances of). Fixed by replacing every such
comparison with a new `assert_files_byte_equal_redacted` helper that
redacts a field's VALUE directly in the RAW file text (never a parsed
Value) and compares the resulting strings byte-for-byte. A new permanent
test, `byte_level_comparison_catches_key_order_divergence_that_value_equality_misses`,
proves both halves of the finding: parsed-Value equality really is
order-blind on this build, and the new byte-level comparator correctly
flags the same pair as divergent.
Red-first evidence for all four fixes (bug reintroduced, test run, failure
quoted, reverted, re-run green) is in this cap's `verification_evidence`
(`red_failure_evidence` field) and the report.

checks.evidence: All five rig elements real, not comment-only. seed_root() copies .bee/bin/lib + hooks + onboarding.json into a tempdir then asserts sha256 equality over 13 paths (both hooks, adapter.mjs, every lib module the hooks dynamically import); the runner executes the seeded, sha256-verified copy. Node-leg non-triviality: every silence fixture's twin makes a positive assertion on node's own stdout, so a silently no-opping node leg fails. Negative control: an independent is_seeded_valid() verifier, with an unseeded tempdir asserted DETECTED invalid. Twin pairing on 4 of 6 behavioural tests. Meta-proof wraps assert_process_conformant in catch_unwind and requires it to panic on a deliberately divergent pair. seed_crash_root doctors a dependency but re-asserts the sha256 of adapter.mjs and both hook files afterwards, so the unit under diff is never doctored.

Silence classes are genuinely proven on BOTH runtimes (assert_process_conformant compares node.status==rust.status and trimmed stdout, so explicit empties bind both legs), and covered trigger classes are compared byte-for-byte as strings, not parsed JSON. GAP: the cell action names the worker-collect nudge as firing 'when a bee worker OR swarming phase', but no fixture ever seeds state.workers (rg for 'workers' in the rig returns nothing). Every nudge fixture triggers via phase=swarming only, so chain_nudge.rs:124 is_registered_worker and the whole ported worker_name() fallback ladder (chain_nudge.rs:62-77, mirroring bee-chain-nudge.mjs:36-47) is never diffed against the oracle. Related: no chain-nudge fixture passes session_id, so state::resolve_pipeline is never exercised — the phase always comes from the readState fallback.

LOCK_BUSY is genuine: a real background thread takes bee_core::lock::with_store_lock(root,'state') on the same named lock file the mjs hook contends with maxAttempts:1 — no flag, no stub — and it is load-bearing because the identical seeded shape WITHOUT a holder does rebuild. Silence and exit 0 asserted on both legs. msn-7 F8 holds by construction (no workflow writer exists in state_projection.rs). THREE gaps: (a) no workflow record is ever seeded, so list_workflows() is always empty and every state-sync fixture lands in the workflows.is_empty() apply_overrides_only fall-through — the authoritative rebuild branches this cell exists to route through are never diffed against node, and state_sync_idle_bootstrap_rebuild_matches_oracle does not construct the branch its name claims. (b) The hold row is the only one of the four renewed records with no cross-runtime comparison; holds.rs renew_holds round-trips through the typed Hold struct (eight Option fields, no skip_serializing_if) — exactly the shape of the bug this cell caught elsewhere, guarded only by prose. (c) Side-effect parity compares parsed serde_json::Values; with preserve_order on, Value equality is IndexMap equality, which is order-INSENSITIVE — key-order and formatting divergence in written store files is invisible to this rig, despite D3 being a byte-compatibility decision. Only stdout is truly byte-compared.

Both legs crash for real. Node: the seeded state.mjs is overwritten with a hookEnabled() that throws, and both hooks' first in-try call is stateLib.hookEnabled, so a real Error is thrown inside the try and caught by logCrash. Rust: BEE_QUEEN_BEE_CRASH_SEAM arms a genuine panic!() unwinding through catch_unwind in run_fail_open, reached from both new hooks. Tests assert exit 0, empty stdout, no partial state.json, and a hooks.jsonl line naming the fault on all four combinations. Judge re-ran the target: 16 passed.

The crash line's CONTENT is not node-conformant and the rig cannot see it. run_fail_open (crates/queen-bee/src/hooks/write_guard.rs:692) logs adapter::log_crash(root, HOOK_NAME, ..) where HOOK_NAME is the file-level const 'write-guard' (write_guard.rs:56). chain_nudge.rs:40 and state_sync.rs:51 both call that same helper, so a chain-nudge or state-sync panic writes "hook":"write-guard" into .bee/logs/hooks.jsonl while the node oracle writes the real hook name (adapter.mjs logCrash emits hook: hookName). The two crash tests only assert on the error substring and never compare the node and rust log lines to each other, so the divergence passes green. Pre-existing from rust-port-10 (model_guard.rs has the same call) but newly extended to two more hooks by this cell; fix is to thread the caller's hook name into run_fail_open.

Judge's own run: 16 passed (1 suite, 0.53s); --list confirms 16 tests named per class across chain-nudge silence/trigger/crash, state-sync throttle/disabled/lock-busy/renewal/rebuild/crash, plus rig self-check, diff-detector and negative control. No test is vacuous in the asserts-nothing sense: the disabled-hook and throttled-no-op fixtures seed a genuinely stale (120s) / genuinely fresh (5s) session against a real 60s throttle and assert byte-equal before/after on both legs. One honesty defect: state_sync_idle_bootstrap_rebuild_matches_oracle names a branch it does not construct. METHOD LIMIT, disclosed by the judge: the mandated out-of-tree mutation experiment could not be run because this environment's bee-write-guard denied every Bash command with a write target outside the worktree (reproduced on a bare mkdir), so the two load-bearing proofs are static-deterministic rather than executed.

The fix is real and its regression guard is genuine for the session record: heartbeat_session reads the raw Value, inserts last_heartbeat and writes it back with no typed struct in the write path; renew_claim_ttl does the same on the raw claim value. The hazard was real (Session declares lane/transcript_path as Option with no skip_serializing_if, while claims.mjs createSession never emits lane and conditionally spreads transcript_path). The guard asserts full-object equality of node and rust session.json with only last_heartbeat and started_at redacted, and serde_json Map equality requires equal length, so a revert to the typed round-trip fails deterministically. Weaker by construction: the claim-side assert (its fixture writes all three struct-named fields, so a typed round-trip would inject no null), and the hold record — the remaining typed round-trip — has no cross-runtime assert at all.

No .remove( / swap_remove / Map::remove appears in the added lines of ab27bef, nor anywhere in the new hooks, the new bee-core write paths, or the rig. Every mutation on the new write paths is either Map::insert on an already-present key (position-preserving under IndexMap) or an in-place struct field assignment. One order-adjacent observation, not a remove hazard: HoldsStore serializes `holds` before its flattened extras, so a ledger whose on-disk order placed an unknown top-level key first would be rewritten with holds first — unreachable via the current writers, and invisible to the rig anyway because its comparisons are order-insensitive parsed Values.

The commit touches no packages/bee, no crates/Cargo.toml members edit, no .bee/bin edit; the only .bee path is the cell record. Hooks stay dark: nothing in .codex/hooks.json, .bee/bin/hooks/*.mjs or .bee/config.json references queen-bee — registration is confined to the in-crate dispatcher. Live store untouched: every fixture root is a tempfile::tempdir(), the negative control runs with cwd in a tempdir where root discovery finds no .bee, and git status on .bee/state.json is empty after the judge's own suite run.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: state-sync side-effect parity never seeds a workflow record (rebuild proven only on the empty-workflow fall-through) and never compares the hold row across runtimes; chain-nudge's registered-worker trigger branch has no fixture; rust crash lines log hook="write-guard" where node logs the real hook name; and store-file parity is compared as order-insensitive parsed Values under a byte-compatibility decision.
